question.problem:
Let $⟨-1,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x+5y=k \\ 2x-y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=-13$

II. $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=-1$

III. $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=13$
question.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3-10 \\  & -13.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -1 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|}{-13} \\ |\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}| & =(-1)(-13) \\ |\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}| & =13\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".
